summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for high-dose Cytoxan and stem cell mobilization as part of treatment for multiple myeloma. Prior to chemotherapy, a urinalysis revealed evidence of a urinary tract infection, including positive nitrites and elevated white blood cells, despite the absence of urinary symptoms. Chemotherapy was withheld as a precaution, and the patient was discharged home with a seven-day course of levofloxacin. The urine culture later indicated mixed bacterial flora, consistent with contamination, but treatment was maintained due to the initial findings and the need to ensure safety before immunosuppressive therapy. The patient also has multiple comorbidities including COPD, atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, abdominal aortic aneurysm, and a history of bladder cancer with neo-bladder reconstruction. He was stable at discharge with plans to reschedule chemotherapy after completing antibiotics.
